body_markdown:
The people closest to a business problem often know what needs to change, but haven’t always had the tools to change it themselves. AI is giving more of them the ability to turn that knowledge into working software, shortening the distance between identifying a problem and solving it.


Making that possible across a company means connecting AI to the data, tools, and systems people already use.


In[The Rise of the Self-Driving Company](https://replit.com/blog/rise-of-self-driving-company) , Amjad Masad, CEO of Replit, describes a future in which people set direction, exercise judgment, and remain accountable while agents take on more execution. Getting there means giving people the ability to act on their expertise, alongside clear boundaries for the systems and data agents can use.


At Microsoft Ignite, we’re expanding our collaboration with Microsoft to help teams create software with the data and tools their business already uses. Today we are excited about enabling three core integrations with Microsoft: Our integration with Microsoft Fabric and Local Work on Windows and Microsoft Teams integration are becoming generally available, alongside early access to Azure deployment options.


In addition, we’re proud to be named the 2026 Microsoft Partner of the Year for Startups.


## Turn business expertise into working applications


### Generally available: Integration with Microsoft Fabric


Following its public preview in June,[Replit’s integration with Microsoft Fabric](https://replit.com/blog/microsoft-fabric) is now generally available, giving enterprises a direct path from describing an application in natural language to deploying it within their organization’s Fabric tenant. Teams can build operational dashboards, reporting interfaces, and department-specific tools while maintaining existing per-user access controls and security policies.


> “Integrating Replit with Microsoft’s data, developer tools, and workplace experiences, helps businesses put AI-powered software creation into the hands of the people closest to the work, while keeping people in control.”


*Sachin Patney, Vice President, App Development, Microsoft.*


Using Rayfin, a Microsoft open-source SDK and CLI, Replit scaffolds application backends with data models, authentication, and access policies. Teams can securely connect to governed Fabric data sources and deploy applications directly into their organization’s Fabric tenant.


For enterprises already invested in Fabric, this extends the platform’s value from data and analytics to the applications teams use to run their business. Developers spend less time building and maintaining custom application infrastructure and deployment pipelines, while business teams can turn governed data into usable tools.


> “We appreciate how quickly we can build and iterate in Replit, but for some of our business, our data needs to stay governed and centralized in Fabric. With Rayfin, we finally have both.”


*Cody Luth, AI Solutions Architect, Leatherman*


[Learn more about Replit and Microsoft Fabric.](https://replit.com/blog/microsoft-fabric)


Enterprise data is one starting point. The projects people already work on and the conversations where they identify problems are others.


## Bring Replit Agent into the places work already happens


### Generally available: Local Work on Windows


Local access is now generally available in Replit Desktop app on Windows, Mac, and Linux. Choose which folders Replit can access, describe what you want to build or change, and review the results locally.


These local environments use sandboxing powered by Microsoft Execution Containers. Local apps and automations can leverage local inference using Microsoft Foundry Local models, which run directly on-device with no cloud round-trip and no data leaving the machine, as well as NVIDIA CUDA-accelerated models.


[Explore Replit Desktop.](https://replit.com/desktop)


### Generally available: Replit in Microsoft Teams


Work often starts in a team conversation: a question, a feature request, or a decision about what to do next. Acting on it can mean moving to another tool and explaining the context again.


Our Teams integration lets people ask Replit questions, investigate, and start work from team conversations, with a handoff to Replit on the web when needed. The goal is to shorten the path from discussing a problem to doing something about it, bringing Replit into the place where teams already collaborate.


## Deploy in your cloud, with Replit’s simplicity


### Available in early access: Publish apps to Azure


Replit is available in Microsoft Marketplace which allows Azure customers to build with Replit and publish applications directly into their company’s Microsoft Azure tenant. Replit provisions and manages the hosting infrastructure, while administrators control the publishing destination for each workspace. For builders, the experience stays familiar: click “Publish” to deploy.


Published apps can connect to private databases in the company’s Azure environment, with access configurable through the company network or VPN. Security teams can use their existing cloud security tools to inspect deployed workloads and dependencies. Development remains on Replit in this configuration.


### Next: Build and run on Azure with Full BYOC


Full BYOC will bring compute, storage, the file system, integrations, and Replit’s Agent harness into your Azure environment alongside your published applications. Teams will be able to build with internal systems and company data while security teams govern which resources the Agent can reach and apply controls to outbound connections.


Replit will manage the infrastructure, preserving the familiar building experience while giving your organization greater isolation and control across development and production.


[Learn more about Bring Your Own Cloud](https://replit.com/blog/bring-your-own-cloud) .


## More people building where their business works


These launches are the reasons Replit was named the 2026 Microsoft Partner of the Year for Startups.


Replit’s solutions bring customers closer to the data, files, conversations, and infrastructure teams already use. They are practical steps toward the Self-Driving Company: people set direction and apply their expertise, while agents take on more execution.


As companies delegate more, they need clear boundaries around what agents can access, which actions require approval, and how people review the results.


[Explore Replit for your organization.](https://replit.com/enterprise)
